newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Congo stability more important than elections.
newsitem.headline: Congo stability more important than elections.

text.p: European Development Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro said on Wednesday the new leader of the former Zaire was right to concentrate on consolidating his rule before holding democratic elections.

"The fact that Mr (Laurent) Kabila promised to have a new constitution and elections within two years is understandable. Time is required to stabilise the government," Deus Pinheiro told the European Parliament.
"Rather wait and have a good electoral process (than) rush and have a corrupt electoral process," the Portuguese commissioner added.
His remarks followed angry reactions from opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi and his supporters to Kabila's refusal to give Tshisekedi the post of prime minister in a new broad-based government.

Deus Pinheiro said he agreed with President Mandela of South Africa that Kabila's "first priority is law and order and stabilisation", following the ousting from power of former President Mobutu Sese Seko by Kabila's rebel alliance.

But he warned that a two year delay in elections was "the upper limit" for the European Union and said that while the West should not demonise Kabila "we must be sure we are not running away from a dictator to autocratic rule".

The EU remained extremely concerned by reports of rebel attacks on Rwandan refugees caught up in the civil war which led to the toppling of Mobutu after 32 years of repressive and corrupt rule, Deus Pinheiro said.

Peace and stability in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo was vital to prevent an explosion of violence and political instability in the whole central African region,he added, citing smouldering conflicts in Congo-Brazzaville, the Central African Republic, Angola, Sudan, Rwanda and Burundi.
